summary: HydraNet sustained throughput collapse and streaming churn during EOD peak — customer escalation and restoration plan
description:
Issue summary:
At ~2026-03-10 13:20 UTC HydraNet (enterprise customer, heavy EOD ingest) observed a sudden throughput collapse on our hosted endpoint with a concurrent surge in 5xx responses and streaming connection churn. Customer-facing symptom: stalled streaming responses and partial transcripts, causing downstream ingestion failures for HydraNet's reconciliation pipeline.

Impact:
- Duration: ~13:20 UTC to 15:05 UTC (services gradually recovered after mitigation).
- Affected keys: HydraNet production account only (single-customer outage).
- Observable metrics: request success rate dropped to 64% at the peak; median token latency increased from 60ms to 450ms; streaming disconnects increased by 8x.
- Business impact: HydraNet reported delayed reconciliation jobs and customer SLAs missed for two internal teams.

Detection timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-10 13:18 UTC: Automatic SLO alert — sustained tail latency increase for prod us-east serving runtime.
- 13:20 UTC: HydraNet support message escalated to #support and #incidents.
- 13:28 UTC: On-call SRE triage — observed GPU pool evictions and autoscaler churn.
- 13:35 UTC: Streaming subsystem began reporting protocol-level disconnects correlated with high write latencies to KV cache.
- 14:05 UTC: Engineering confirmed a recently deployed kernel-selection optimization (serving-runtime PR 7421) had started rolling at 13:10 UTC and coincided with increased memory pressure on certain model variants.
- 14:25 UTC: Temporary routing change applied for HydraNet to reserved spillover capacity; errors and disconnects dropped noticeably.
- 15:05 UTC: Rollback of kernel-selection rollout and autoscaler headroom increase completed; service metrics returned to baseline.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Simulate HydraNet workload pattern: long prompt prefixes with many concurrent streams (~180 concurrent long-poll streams) and high token emission.
2) Push the kernel-selection optimization and observe memory/KV pressure under sustained concurrent prefix reuse.
3) Monitor autoscaler reaction and GPU pool eviction rates.

Logs & artifacts:
- Obs dashboard: https://observability.redwood.ai/d/serving/hydranet-20260310
- Kernel rollout PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/7421
- Autoscaler changelog PR: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/198
- Sample log snippets captured in S3: s3://redwood-incidents/2026/223456/log-snippets.txt

Investigation notes (summary):
- Initial hypothesis: noisy neighbor / GPU exhaustion. Partially true: a combination of GPU pool saturation and unexpectedly long pod startup times caused by a change in kernel selection that increased per-process memory footprint for redwood/gpt-13b-v2-quantized.
- Autoscaler behavior: configured headroom was insufficient for the rapid EOD concurrency spike. The autoscaler attempted scale-up but pod startup latency (7–12s) combined with queueing resulted in amplified 5xx rates and connection timeouts.
- KV cache interaction: greater memory pressure led to higher eviction rates in the KV store for streaming sessions, which manifested as mid-stream disconnects and resume failures.
- Root cause (contributing factors):
  * Rollout of kernel-selection heuristics (PR 7421) increased resident memory for a subset of quantized model variants.
  * Autoscaler headroom and scale-up thresholds were too conservative for HydraNet's bursty EOD profile.
  * Lack of a dedicated canary window for kernel-selection across high-concurrency enterprise customers.

Workaround & mitigation applied during incident:
- Immediate actions: routed HydraNet traffic to reserved spillover capacity and temporarily increased per-customer concurrency caps. Rolled back kernel-selection optimization for affected variants. Increased autoscaler target headroom for the us-east GPU pool.
- Customer communication: CS provided live updates every 30 minutes and offered a temporary service credit pending post-incident review.

Resolution:
- Rollback of kernel-selection rollout completed at 15:05 UTC; traffic normalized after autoscaler scaled to the increased headroom.
- Confirmed by synthetic checks and HydraNet validation tests at 15:22 UTC. Full incident declared mitigated and later marked resolved after verification.

Post-incident action items (owners assigned):
- Engineering: add a canary gating policy for kernel-selection rollouts that includes a synthetic high-concurrency workload (owner: Marco Ruiz, due 2026-03-21).
- Autoscaler: revise default headroom for enterprise customers and introduce per-customer cap overrides (owner: Priya Desai, due 2026-03-18).
- Observability: add a composite alert for concurrent increases in pod startup latency + KV eviction rate to detect similar regressions earlier (owner: Liam O'Connor, due 2026-03-16).
- SRE/On-call runbook: update hydra/hotpath playbook with explicit spillover routing steps and contact matrix (owner: SRE team, due 2026-03-19).
- CS & Account: finalize customer credit and post-incident customer-facing summary (owner: Emily Zhao, due 2026-03-12 — completed).

Follow-ups:
- Engineering will open a targeted performance optimization PR for the quantized variant to reduce resident memory (tracking PR planned: serving-runtime/pull/7510).
- Schedule a joint postmortem review with HydraNet on 2026-03-17.

Notes:
- Incident was single-customer impacting but exposed a rollout risk that could affect other enterprise customers under similar concurrency patterns. Action items prioritize safety of rollouts and autoscaler policy updates.
